I picked up a trowel that lay on the ground, its worn edge a testament to its long use, and began to examine it more closely. The bright metal seemed almost out of place against the dull, cracked glass that surrounded us. Nearby, a twine lay discarded on the floor, and I'd picked that up as well, curiosity getting the better of me. The furnace to the north beckoned, its presence a constant reminder of the work that needed to be done, while the colonnade to the east seemed to stretch out endlessly.
